title: Audit an existing email flow before rewriting; next-step onboarding
decision_task: When an owner has a running flow, ClimbOS first maps it and scores per-email performance and sending practices, protects what works, and only then rewrites. / Which onboarding emails a trial or new-account flow needs: one next step per email triggered by what the user has or hasn't done, plus a usage recap and a 'where did you get stuck' question for inactive users.
applies_when: Owner connects an ESP with an existing automation
Request to 'improve my emails' or 'fix my welcome flow'
SaaS, app, membership or booking-portal onboarding
exclusions: No existing flow (write fresh per lifecycle-email)
Fewer than ~100 recipients per email (metrics too noisy; audit structure only)
No event data (fall back to time-based with clear labelling)
One-off service purchases with no product use (use post-purchase type instead)
evidence_requirements: Flow export or screenshots: triggers, delays, branches, tags
Per-email recipients, clicks, conversions, unsubscribes, complaints, attributed revenue
Events available to the ESP (did X, did not do Y)
missing_data_behavior: Fewer than ~100 recipients per email: audit structure only, not performance.
No event data: time-based emails, labelled as such; no usage recap.
alternatives_when_constrained: No customers yet: no flow to audit; build fresh
Low traffic: structural audit only; judge on replies and conversions over a longer window
No customers yet: build the flow from the product's own steps; mark windows as assumptions
Low traffic: judge on replies and activation counts, not rates

decision_branches.then: Map it, find contacts with no next step, mark each email protect / fix / queue, then rewrite.

decision_branches.if: Inactive trial users with event data
decision_branches.then: One 'where did you get stuck?' email and a usage recap.

implementation_steps: Map the flow outside the ESP: triggers, delays, branches, action and inaction triggers, exits
Find black holes: contacts who finish or stall with no next step
Record per-email click rate, conversion rate, unsubscribe and complaint rates, revenue per recipient; treat opens as a deliverability hint only
Classify: protect (clear standouts), fix first (high unsubscribe or complaints, no exit on conversion, broken consent), queue (cadence, too many or too few segments, dead ends)
Audit sending: SPF, DKIM, DMARC, one-click unsubscribe, real reply-to, postal address, list hygiene
Report to owner before any rewrite; rewrite only red emails first, keeping green ones as controls
Define the activation event and the 2 to 4 steps before it
One email per missing step, triggered by its absence, with one CTA
For users inactive after N days, send a plain question asking where they got stuck (open, not yes/no)
Send a usage recap (what they did, one thing they missed) when data supports it
Exit on activation; move to conversion or value emails
metrics: Clicks, conversions and revenue per recipient per email
Number of black-hole contacts before and after
guardrails: No rewrite of a green email without the owner's say-so
No open-rate targets; opens are distorted by Apple Mail Privacy Protection
Read-only access; never send or edit flows without explicit approval
Last-touch revenue is labelled as over-crediting late emails
Recaps only from real usage data, never estimated
Don't cite the study's shares or third-party churn stats as facts in copy
observation_window: Baseline: last 30 and 90 days. After changes: 30 days or a pre-set number of conversions. / One full trial length plus 14 days per cohort.
stop_conditions: Complaint rate reaches 0.3%: stop sends and review list and consent
No conversion data available: audit structure and deliverability only, and say so
Stuck-question emails get complaints: soften cadence
Activation flat after 2 cohorts: revisit the activation definition with the owner
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes
climbos_location: skills/lifecycle-email/SKILL.md (new 'optimise an existing flow' mode before step 5) / skills/lifecycle-email/SKILL.md sequence table (Onboarding row) and step 5

interpretation: LABELLED INTERPRETATION: lifecycle-email covers writing new flows well, but has no mode for diagnosing an existing one. The Copyhackers audit order (map, measure, classify, then rewrite) fills that gap.

LABELLED INTERPRETATION: the 127-trial study shows what companies send (from one mostly inactive recipient), not what performs. It is useful as a gap signal (few send usage recaps), not as a benchmark.
proposed_climbos_rule: PROPOSED RULE: when an existing flow is connected, lifecycle-email must output a flow map, a per-email protect/fix/queue table and a deliverability checklist before any new copy.
PROPOSED RULE: the lifecycle-email onboarding row adds 'stuck question' and 'usage recap' as optional jobs, both gated on real event data.
disagreements: Copyhackers uses a day-zero open-rate threshold (<40%) as a red flag. ClimbOS ignores opens as a success metric and should not adopt that threshold; at most, a sharp drop in opens is a deliverability hint.
None material. The article leans on secondhand statistics, which ClimbOS should not reuse.
